articles.title: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham: Olivia Smith stunner saves Gunners from shocking defeat but pressure intensifies on Renee Slegers
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Arsenal draw 1-1 with Birmingham City at the Emirates Stadium; Olivia Smith's stunner cancels out Oceane Hurtre's opener; Arsenal with just one win in six WSL games
articles.body:
Arsenal went into the international break with just five points from their opening five WSL games after the 4-2 defeat with Manchester City, and just one win in six in all competitions.

A home game against newly-promoted Birmingham, who themselves had mustered just two league draws all campaign, seemed like the scenario to return to winning ways.

After Alessia Russo struck the post with a fabulous diving header in the first half, the Gunners were left stunned as they were hit on the break early in the second, allowing September's player of the month Oceane Hurtre to poke the visitors ahead.

Birmingham's resolve was tested, with Sophie Baggaley making a superb save to maintain the lead. However, seconds later she was beaten by an incredible Olivia Smith strike to pull Slegers' side level.

Arsenal pushed for a late winner but a combination of Baggaley and their inefficiency in front of goal that has plagued them all season ensured they went winless in five WSL games for the first time.

It resulted in boos at the full-time whistle, as questions over Slegers' future intensify.

14: SAVE! Cooney-Cross' smart half-volley kept out by Baggaley.

18: OVER! Russo gifted a chance after Baggaley's poor pass, but attempted lob goes over.

38: POST! Russo comes agonisingly close to converting excellent Williamson cross.

50: OVER! Holmberg impressive run ends in her striking over the bar.

53: GOAL! Arsenal shell-shocked as Hurtre gives Birmingham lead on the counter.

65: HUGE SAVE! Baggaley denies Baum from point-blank range.

66: GOAL! Smith stunner pulls Gunners level.

73: MASSIVE SAVE! Baggaley again on hand to stop Wubben-Moy right on the line.

76: OVER! Smith snatches at big chance to put Arsenal ahead.

Slegers: If I can't help the team, a change is needed

Arsenal boss Renee Slegers speaking in her post-match press conference:

"Everything I want is for the best of us and for the success of all these players. So, that's heavily on my mind and I still believe I can impact and help the team forward.

"But, if that's not the case anymore, then a change needs to happen, but I have belief in knowing where we can go with this team and it's been really tough.

"Like I just said, if it had been all negative and we hadn't been looking like Arsenal but that's not the case.

"There's some details that we need to get right and those details are costing us right now. Those margins are costing us and I believe that if we get that right, it'll be good."

"It's been such an interesting start to the season for Arsenal. I think they are left with so many questions and no answers right now, but they are not playing badly. They're not failing to create chances.

"If Manchester City and Chelsea win tomorrow, you would almost write them out of the title race.

"If they had won today they might've found a bit of momentum. I genuinely think the failure to win today has pushed them out of a title race. That was not what Renee Slegers' mission was this season."

articles.body: Julien Escudé es uno de los integrantes del último Sevilla que fue capaz de ganarle al Real Madrid en el Santiago Bernabéu. "Recuerdo que en aquella época teníamos una buena dinámica por todo lo que estábamos logrando, el aspecto anímico positivo es muy importante para objetivos como ganar en el Bernabéu. Son campos donde es difícil ganar, se necesita una gran solidez mental y física colectiva", dijo el ex central en los micrófonos de 'Sólo el Sevilla'. ¿Cómo ve el francés al Sevilla de García Plaza? "El arranque ha sido bastante positivo después de varios años con dificultades, es la base para la ilusión de poder ganar allí. También tenemos en la memoria el buen partido que hizo el Sevilla ante el Barça en el Sánchez-Pizjuán, con un gran espíritu competitivo. Fuera de casa tiene argumentos, como la solidaridad, la intensidad y la confianza necesaria para enfrentarse a un Real Madrid que todavía no ha despegado", apuntó. Un buen momento. "El Madrid lleva varias temporadas sin ganar títulos y eso no es fácil allí. Ahora el Barça le está poniendo el nivel muy alto y tiene la obligación de estar a esa altura. Tiene nuevo entrenador y nuevos jugadores que tienen que encajar en el modelo, pero siempre es un peligro en su campo, donde apenas deja puntos. El Sevilla tiene que ser compacto, intenso, comprometido y rocoso, y luego tener eficacia arriba, claro. Puede ser un buen momento para ir al Bernabéu". Optimista. "El Sevilla ha construido este año una plantilla al menos para no sufrir. Un buen arranque es clave y si la plantilla se lo cree pues se ven cosas mucho más positivas. Partiendo de la base de volver a hacer un fortín en casa y tener una dinámica de sumar puntos fuera. Veo a un Sevilla que limita los errores, más maduro, más hecho, con gente que conoce LaLiga y que hace buen vestuario. Se puede construir un futuro. Lo principal es la solidez defensiva, desde el portero y los centrales hasta arriba, tener oficio y sin miedo, porque eso tranquiliza al equipo". Los centrales del Sevilla. "Los centrales me encantan, canteranos que se dejan el alma. Kike Salas ha madurado mucho, tiene fe, potencia y toma mejores decisiones. Castrín tiene una gran actitud y salida de balón". Con acento francés. "Stassin cumple con lo que necesita el Sevilla, un delantero guerrero, potente y luchador cuando futbolísticamente no son están las cosas fáciles. Lo veo a gusto, con fe y ganas. Félix ha aprendido mucho en el Lille, que trabaja bien con los jóvenes. Fofana es un jugador de un gran calibre y creo que ha llegado a un club donde va a ser importante y en una gran liga como la española. Tiene perfil de 6, de 8 y más variantes, es muy profesional y se informó bien del Sevilla para no equivocarse. Agoumé está teniendo continuidad y mejora con lo que lo rodea, está creciendo en confianza y está rindiendo muy bien".

articles.standfirst: El relevo en el banquillo, con la llegada de Nicola, le sentó bien a los recién ascendidos
articles.summary: El relevo en el banquillo, con la llegada de Nicola, le sentó bien a los recién ascendidos
articles.body: A entrenador nuevo, victoria segura. El recién ascendido Venezia ha hecho bueno el dicho ante el Nápoles (1-0). Se marchó Giovanni Stroppa y llegó Davide Nicola. Un relevo que otorgó a los 'arancioneroverdi', que habían perdido sus seis partidos hasta la fecha, sus primeros tres puntos en la Serie A. Los de Allegri, por su parte, son novenos con 10 puntos, a seis de Inter y Lazio. Repitió Allegri con defensa de tres, pero esta vez sin Rafa Marín, suplente. No hubo demasiadas ocasiones hasta el descanso, pero las mejores fueron para el 'Napoli': un tiro de Giovane desde 25 metros salió rozando la escuadra y Rrahmani vio cómo le taponaban un remate 'in extremis' en el 30'. A la salida de vestuarios, en el 49', llegó el 1-0. Se durmió Rrahmani y lo aprovechó Akor Adams para robarle la cartera. El ex del Sevilla le ganó un balón dividido y conectó un disparo que desvió lo justo el propio Rrahmani para despistar a Meret. Cuatro goles, dos en Liga, ya Adams. Reaccionó bien el Nápoles. Juan Jesus sacó sobre la línea en el 59' un centro de Alisson Santos que el recién ingresado Hojlund se disponía a embocar. Volvería a ser protagonista Hojlund en el 68'. El ex del Manchester United forzó un penalti comentido por Matías Moreno. Sin embargo, Filip Stankovic adivinó el lanzamiento desde los 11 metros de Kevin de Bruyne, que la semana pasada materializó contra el Frosinone, en la repetición, una pena máxima que había fallado De Bruyne. Resistió bien el Venezia, comandado por un omnipresente Kike Pérez. El ex del Valladolid, titular, fue el jugador que más kilómetros recorrió. Incluso pudo hacer el 2-0 Rrahmani en el 74'... pero Meret abortó el contragolpe. El 'MVP', en cualquier caso', fue para Filip Stankovic.El hijo de Dejan se lució para sacar un disparo de Lobotka en el 84' y desviar un disparo abajo de Alisson en el 90'. Dos paradones que otorgan al recién ascendido Venezia sus primeros puntos en la presente Serie A.

articles.title: Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez rushed to hospital after sickening collision at Everton
articles.summary: Martinez received treatment for around 10 minutes after a nasty clash of heads with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite
articles.body:
Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez was rushed to hospital but is "conscious" after a sickening collision with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite .

The players clashed heads as Martinez came off his line to collect an aerial cross into the Everton box, with Branthwaite attempting to attack the ball.

There was immediate concern for both players as they stayed down in the box, but Branthwaite was able to return to his feet after a couple of minutes.

Martinez, however, stayed down on his back as Chelsea physios and medical staff worked with caution and the stretcher was called.

The Argentinian received oxygen on the pitch and was eventually carried off on a stretcher around 10 minutes after the collision.

Broadcaster TNT Sports, who decided against showing a close-up replay of the gruesome clash of heads, reported that Martinez was immediately taken to a local hospital in Liverpool.

But the goalkeeper appeared to be moving his arms while he was stretchered straight down the tunnel, in what looked to be a positive sign.

Speaking to TNT Sports immediately after the match, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said: "As far as I know, he left the stadium conscious.

"Right now he's in the hospital doing precautionary tests. So let's see, but this is what I know so far."

Martinez was replaced in the 73rd minute by Belgian reserve goalkeeper Mike Penders, who came on to make his Premier League debut with Chelsea leading 1-0.

Branthwaite was cleared to continue for Everton after team physios performed concussion checks on the pitch.

When play resumed, Pedro Neto scored his second goal of the game to double Chelsea's lead and seal a 2-0 victory on Merseyside for their first away win of the season.

It also meant that Chelsea kept a clean sheet in the Premier League for the first time in nine months, or since a 2-0 win over Brentford on 17 January.

But the victory was overshadowed by Martinez's injury and the thoughts of Chelsea's players immediately turned to their team-mate.

Match-winner Neto dedicated Chelsea's win and clean sheet to Martinez. The Portuguese forward told TNT Sports: "We are really pleased. It is a shame for Emi but we wish him all the best. This win is for him. We are really happy but of course our thoughts are for him.

"It's in his honour. We needed a clean sheet. We needed a good game. Emi deserved this. Mike [Penders] who came in deserved this as well. So we are really happy."

Martinez, a World Cup winner with Argentina in 2022, was making just his sixth appearance for Chelsea after joining the Blues from Aston Villa in August.

Martinez was stretchered off the pitch following around 10 minutes of treatment (Getty)

articles.title: Spalletti: ‘I’m not irritable enough, quicksand around Juventus’
articles.summary: Luciano Spalletti insists he ‘hasn’t been irritable enough’ with Juventus and hits out at the media for creating ‘quicksand’ around the team ahead of their c...
articles.body:
Luciano Spalletti insists he 'hasn't been irritable enough' with Juventus and hits out at the media for creating 'quicksand' around the team ahead of their clash with Lazio.

It kicks off at the Allianz Juventus Stadium in Turin on Sunday at 19.45 UK time (20.45 CEST).

The Bianconeri are coming off a morale-boosting 2-1 Europa League comeback win away to Celta Vigo , maintaining their 100 per cent record in the competition.

It's a different scenario in Serie A, where they managed just one win, two draws and a defeat in the last four rounds.

Spalletti sees quicksand around Juventus

VIGO, SPAIN – OCTOBER 15: Luciano Spalletti, Head Coach of Juventus, reacts during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Real Club Celta and Juventus at Estadio Balaidos on October 15, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

"I feel that we ought to underline the great work done by Gennaro Gattuso at Lazio, especially considering what was said about him and the team going into the campaign," said Spalletti in his press conference.

"I think he's been the most impressive coach so far along with Massimiliano Alvini at Frosinone and Cagliari's Fabio Pisacane. He has found their identity, and has individual talents like Davide Frattesi who can surge forward from midfield. I know him well and what he can do."

Juventus need some squad rotation after the strain of that trip to Vigo, as Spalletti reveals they only got back at 4.30am on Friday.

"Some of our players can't sleep on plans. In physical terms, we didn't do anything in training either yesterday or today, so we just had to list what to keep an eye on.

"The trouble is you have no idea how the recovery process goes."

TURIN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 17: Luciano Spalletti, Manager of Juventus, reacts during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Juventus and N.E.C. Nijmegen at Juventus Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Spalletti will be forced to watch the match from the stands tomorrow, as he sits out a ban after his altercation with Cagliari coach Pisacane.

"I was not tense, I just have selective fondness for people," smiled the coach.

"Perhaps sometimes I need to be more irritable, and so far I haven't been irritable enough. Feeling that tension allows me to transfer more of it over to my players, because they see and feel my reactions. I would've liked to be ill-tempered…

"Some things were also said that are not fair. I did not go to Pisacane with the intention of arguing, nor did we argue. We looked at each other in an intense way, but I didn't do anything.

"I will watch from the stands and probably speak with my staff at half-time, but I trust the staff I have here at Juventus. I have the best assistant manager in the world, Marco Domenichini."

REGGIO NELL'EMILIA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 13: Luciano Spalletti Head Coach of Juventus looks on prior to the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and Juventus at Mapei Stadium – Citta' del Tricolore on September 13, 2026 in Reggio nell'Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images)

Much has been said about strikers Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani begging to be used together from the start, but Spalletti does not seem ready to make them happy.

"We need to expand the range of starters and divide up the time on the field. Woltemade did well against Celta and, unlike with Cagliari, he managed to put the ball in the net.

"This ability to be ready when opportunity knocks is crucial and rewards those who are most determined. Lazio have two physical centre-backs, so it will be difficult to get through them unless we have bodies in the box."

Juve have won both Europa League games so far this season and it's keeping morale afloat.

"The Europa League helps if you win, because if Juventus don't win games, you get sucked into quicksand all over the place, and we need to be careful where we step," continued Spalletti.

"A team that lives every ball as if it's the one that can change your career, we've got to get deeper into the details too in order to become a unit."

REGGIO NELL'EMILIA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 13: Luciano Spalletti Head Coach of Juventus reacts during the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and Juventus at Mapei Stadium – Citta' del Tricolore on September 13, 2026 in Reggio nell'Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images)

The coach said some things after the Cagliari game that suggested he might be thinking about retirement, but he assured the media that was not the case.

"In every match, we gamble with far more than the result of a single game, but with a chunk of our careers. There are coaches in Serie A this season the same age as my children, and it's good to see youth marching into the future, but don't you worry, I'm not finished yet either.

"I won't stop after Juventus, nor perhaps the job after that, so relax. Those who say I create tension and irritation are those who go against me, and there are many."

There is at least some good news from the medical staff, as Jeremie Boga is available and can play up to 30 minutes.

BERGAMO, ITALY – APRIL 11: Jeremie Boga of Juventus celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and Juventus at Gewiss Stadium on April 11, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images)

"I read and react to what happens, and notice the worst possible slant is given to everything I say…" concluded Spalletti.

"I have been told that I get on and off the bandwagon for Kolo Muani, but mental strength comes from solidity. You need to be prepared to do anything and take risks, and at times you have to go beyond the lines and be a little crazy to go over your level, not to become unpredictable, but to be balanced.

"The way the team reacted against Cagliari and Celta Vigo, that means a lot. I like to share my analysis with the players face to face. This is a solid, healthy side, and I am convinced we'll achieve results, because we are on the right track."

articles.title: Key storylines for Eagles vs. Panthers in Week 6
articles.summary: The Eagles face mounting pressure against the Panthers, and a handful of intriguing storylines may fuel part of the discussion.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles need a response. That's about as plain as it gets. Three consecutive losses have turned what once looked like a manageable stretch into a test of will and heart.

Now, the conversation has shifted. The questions being asked aren't common in the Nick Sirianni coaching era. How does this team steady its ship? How does it regain control of its season? Sunday's matchup with the Carolina Panthers offers an opportunity to stop the slide, but Philadelphia will have to navigate several challenges to take advantage of it.

The Eagles have struggled to protect their quarterback, and last week's trip to London added another layer of concern . The Panthers have vulnerabilities of their own, particularly along the offensive line, but a potential return by a key starter could change that equation. With both teams looking to establish some consistency, several factors could determine how this game unfolds. Here are a few other storylines that may help answer questions in an important Week 6 tussle in the NFC.

Carolina's pass protection is worse than the sack numbers suggest

Bryce Young has taken ten sacks this season, but that number doesn't fully capture the pressure that Carolina's offensive line has allowed. They have surrendered a 42.7% pressure rate. That was the fifth-highest mark in the NFL through the first five weeks. However, Carolina has only played four games.

Taylor Moton's potential return could change Carolina's outlook

One of Carolina's biggest injury storylines involves right tackle Taylor Moton. He has missed the entire season so far while dealing with blood clots. Moton fully participated in practices this week and is listed as questionable, leaving his return to action possible.

His availability would matter beyond the emotional lift of getting a key player back. Moton could strengthen a Panthers offensive line that has struggled to keep pressure away from Young. Philadelphia's pass rush would face a different challenge if Carolina can restore stability at right tackle. That makes Moton's status one of the most consequential developments to monitor before kickoff. He can help improve Carolina's running game and pass protection.

The Eagles could find opportunities against Akayleb Evans

Philadelphia needs to move the ball through the air, and Akayleb Evans could be a favorable matchup. According to Pro Football Focus , Evans has allowed 11 receptions for 197 yards and a touchdown on 14 targets, with opposing quarterbacks recording a 142.6 passer rating when targeting him.

Those numbers suggest the Eagles may have opportunities to attack his coverage. Philadelphia must still be selective with its throws, but avoiding unnecessary risks doesn't mean passing up favorable matchups. Finding ways to exploit Evans could help the Eagles generate air production while easing pressure on the rest of the offense.

An unfavorable scheduling trend adds another challenge

Philadelphia played in London last Sunday before returning to face Carolina, which is coming off a bye. History offers little encouragement for teams facing that particular disadvantage: Teams returning from international games to face opponents coming off a bye are 0-4 in the four documented instances since 2011.

The Buffalo Bills lost to the New York Jets in 2011 after playing in Toronto. The Houston Texans fell to the San Diego Chargers in 2016 after an international game in Mexico City, while the Miami Dolphins lost to the Atlanta Falcons in 2021 after traveling back from London. Last season, the Cleveland Browns lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers following their trip to London.

Across those four games, the international-travel teams averaged just 15.25 points. The sample is small and won't determine what happens Sunday, but it highlights the challenge Philadelphia faces. The Eagles must overcome the demands of travel while preparing for an opponent with extra rest.

A loss would put Nick Sirianni's team in familiar territory

Another Eagles defeat would drop Philadelphia to 2-4. That would match their worst start under Nick Sirianni. He was also 2-4 after six games of his first season in 2021. He handed the play calling to Shane Steichen. A heavy running game was born. The team eventually recovered, finishing 9-8 and reaching the playoffs.

That history reminds us that a difficult start doesn't have to define an entire season. However, the circumstances are different now, and Philadelphia needs to show it can respond to adversity rather than let its early struggles continue. A win over Carolina wouldn't solve every problem, but it would provide much-needed stability. Another loss would deepen the urgency surrounding a season that has already taken several unexpected turns.

articles.title: Confirmed: Barcelona starting lineup against Real Betis – 4 changes as Flick rotates ahead of PSG

FC Barcelona are set to take on Real Betis at La Cartuja in La Liga in less than an hour and Hansi Flick has announced his starting lineup for this evening's encounter.

The Catalans enter the contest looking to maintain their perfect start to the league campaign, having won all eight matches so far this season.

However, the fixture comes during an exceptionally demanding period for Barcelona, following their 4-1 Champions League victory over Galatasaray.

It is sandwiched right inbetween that trip to Turkey and a trip to France to face PSG, before welcoming Real Madrid to the Camp Nou next weekend.

Flick's team selection has attracted particular attention, with the German tactician having to make some difficult calls to manage workload.

In goal, Joan Garcia unsurprisingly starts for Barcelona, while Jules Kounde, Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin and Xavi Espart complete the defensive line.

Moving into midfield, Rodri and Pedri feature alongside Fermin Lopez as Flick looks to establish control against a Betis side capable of causing problems in possession.

Further forward, Lamine Yamal and Karim Adeyemi occupy the wide positions with Gabriel Jesus leading Barca's attack.

The most notable selection decision is starting Karim Adeyemi on the left instead of the in-form Anthony Gordon.

Meanwhile, Jules Kounde replaces Eric at right-back and Gabriel Jesus returns to the starting line-up after a promising cameo against Galatasaray.

With Barcelona facing PSG and Real Madrid in the coming days, Flick's choices also offer an indication of how he intends to manage his squad through this important run of fixtures.

Nevertheless, the immediate priority remains securing another three points and extending Barcelona's outstanding start to the domestic season and it remains to be seen how they fare against Betis.

articles.title: Venezia upset Napoli for first Serie A win of season
articles.summary: Napoli's torrid start to the season continued Saturday when Venezia head coach Davide Nicola masterminded a shock 1-0 win on debut as Kevin De Bruyne had a p...
articles.body:
Napoli's torrid start to the season continued Saturday when Venezia head coach Davide Nicola masterminded a shock 1-0 win on debut as Kevin De Bruyne had a penalty saved.

Renowned survival specialist Nicola was appointed during the week to replace sacked coach Giovanni Stroppa after last season's Serie B champions failed to pick up a single point in their opening six games.

He made an instant impact as Akor Adams struck the winner early in the second half to seal Venezia's first Serie A win over Napoli since 1942.

It marked a second defeat in a row for Massimiliano Allegri's side after their midweek Champions League loss at Villarreal, and their fifth defeat in nine games in all competitions this season.

A flat game came to life early in the second half when Nigeria international Adams latched on to a long ball and beat Alex Meret with a deflected strike in the 49th minute.

Allegri responded by bringing on rested stars Rasmus Hojlund and Kevin De Bruyne and the Danish striker immediately threatened when Juan Jesus denied him a tap-in with a superb goal-line block.

Hojlund won a penalty for Napoli midway through the second half when he was hauled down in the box by Matias Moreno, but De Bruyne's spot-kick was well saved by Filip Stankovic low to his right.

The Venezia goalkeeper, son of former Inter midfielder Dejan Stankovic, was decisive in the closing stages with a string of saves, including spectacular stops to deny Stanislav Lobotka and Alisson Santos.

Napoli are ninth after picking up 10 points from their first seven games, while Venezia remain bottom with three points.

Later on Saturday, league leaders Inter travel to Bologna before Roma host Genoa.

articles.title: 📊 Erling Haaland continues 2026/27 goal glut with historic day vs Ipswich
articles.summary: Well, it would not be a Premier League weekend without a requisite goal-fest from Manchester City's Erling Haaland. Fresh off a World Cup summer with Norway...
articles.body:
Well, it would not be a Premier League weekend without a requisite goal-fest from Manchester City's Erling Haaland.

Fresh off a World Cup summer with Norway and no longer donning his Samson-like locks, the 26-year-old superstar striker has not lost his scoring touch, however, after giving Enzo Maresca's outfit a one-goal cushion heading into the halftime interval at home against Ipswich.

It was a first half that hardly lacked action at the Etihad, with Phil Foden ending his 10-month goal drought to put the Cityzens in the lead on 19 minutes, only for summer signing Daizen Maeda to equalise for the Tractor Boys almost immediately.

Then it was Haaland's turn, heading home from Mateo Kovačić's cross into the box to beat Christian Walton to restore the one-goal advantage.

With that, Haaland hit his seventh league goal across the 2026/27 season, but more impressively, had bagged 11 in his last eight appearances across all competitions up to that point, after being kept quiet against Bournemouth during the opening Premier League weekend.

A second from the prolific frontman saw him reach 100 non-penalty Premier League goals while needing just 139 appearances to achieve that feat faster than anyone in the league's history.

Is Haaland destined for yet another Golden Boot crown? You'd certainly not bet against it.

articles.title: Arsenal star pushing for January exit after recent struggles
articles.summary: Viktor Gyokeres and Arsenal Facing January Crossroads as Exit Talk GrowsArsenal may be heading towards one of the most awkward transfer subplots of the comin...
articles.body:
Viktor Gyokeres and Arsenal Facing January Crossroads as Exit Talk Grows

Arsenal may be heading towards one of the most awkward transfer subplots of the coming window, with Viktor Gyokeres increasingly unsettled and a January move now described as a genuine possibility. According to TeamTalk , the Sweden international is prepared to reassess his future after a rapid change in standing under Mikel Arteta.

The striking part of this developing story is the speed of the shift. Gyokeres arrived from Sporting CP in 2025 amid significant expectation, after Arsenal chose him ahead of Benjamin Sesko. He then delivered in a major way, scoring 21 goals in all competitions, including 14 in the Premier League, and playing his part in a title-winning season as well as a run to the Champions League final.

That return should have strengthened his place. Instead, the current picture appears very different. TeamTalk states that "Viktor Gyokeres is ready to quit Arsenal and is set to push for a January exit", a line that underlines the seriousness of the situation. The report adds that frustration over his minutes is central, with the striker "yet to start a Premier League game this season".

Premier League starts at centre of Arsenal concern

From the player's perspective, the issue seems straightforward. A striker of Gyokeres' profile and age does not want to drift through the first half of a season waiting for opportunities. Sources cited in the report say "his lack of opportunities is the main reason he is now looking towards the exit door", and there is little ambiguity in that.

Arsenal's internal thinking may be more layered. Kai Havertz is "currently the preferred option", while long-term admiration for Julian Alvarez remains active in the background. The report notes that Arsenal's pursuit of Alvarez over the summer was "a development that could not be ignored by Gyokeres and his camp". For a centre-forward already fighting for starts, that pursuit naturally sends a message, whether intended or not.

It is also notable that Arsenal are said to be open to doing more business in attack. TeamTalk reports that the club "could be prepared to consider allowing Gyokeres to leave as they continue pushing ahead with plans to bring in another forward". If that proves accurate, this is no longer a story about one unhappy player alone. It becomes a structural squad decision.

Julian Alvarez interest adds to transfer pressure

Arsenal "remain hugely keen on Alvarez", according to the report, and that ongoing interest appears to be one of the two key drivers behind Gyokeres' current stance, along with the absence of Premier League starts. In practical terms, a striker can accept competition. What becomes harder to accept is the sense that the club may already be planning for somebody else to lead the line.

That is why this situation feels significant. Arsenal "spent months doing their homework on Gyokeres" before completing the move, and Arteta had been clear in wanting him in north London. For that level of planning to lead to this uncertainty little more than a year later would raise fair questions over recruitment alignment and squad planning.

Gyokeres has done his part internationally, too. He "continues to score regularly for Sweden and struck four goals during the recent Nations League international break". That form only sharpens the player's likely belief that he should be starting more often at club level.

Atletico Madrid and Europe monitoring Gyokeres situation

As for the market, Atletico Madrid remain firmly in the frame. TeamTalk says the Spanish club's interest was discussed directly with Arsenal during meetings involving Andrea Berta in the summer. There is also mention of interest from the Premier League, Italy and Germany, suggesting this is not a case of one option or nothing.

Crucially, the pieces do appear to fit. The report says "with the player open to a departure and the club still keen to strengthen their attacking options, a January separation could suit both parties". That may ultimately be the clearest line in the entire update. If both sides see logic in a split, the coming months could be about shaping the right deal rather than preventing an exit.

Arsenal still have time to change the direction of this story. More starts, a clearer role and firmer communication would help. For now, though, Viktor Gyokeres, Arsenal and a possible January transfer are moving into a space worth watching very closely.

From an Arsenal supporter's perspective, this is deeply frustrating because it feels like a familiar problem of our own making. We signed a striker with pedigree, backed him after a long process, watched him score 21 goals in a huge season, then somehow reached a point where "the striker is yet to start a Premier League game this season". That is hard to defend.

If the report is accurate, the most annoying part is the mixed messaging. You cannot push for a player, pick him ahead of other targets, celebrate the decision, then spend the next window chasing another elite forward and expect there to be no consequences. Of course Gyokeres and his camp would question where he stands. Any player would.

There is also a bigger concern for Arsenal here. Elite clubs need strong competition, but they also need clarity. If Kai Havertz is the preferred option, say it through selection. If Gyokeres is genuinely valued, use him properly. Letting a proven goalscorer slide towards the exit after one strong season would feel wasteful and short-sighted.

Supporters will rightly ask why a player who helped deliver the title now seems expendable so quickly. If Arsenal sell in January and then spend heavily again, it will look like another expensive correction rather than a clear plan. That is the part fans will struggle with most.

articles.title: Manolo González: "Se nos va el partido en una situación controlable"
articles.standfirst: El técnico perico lamentó la última acción del encuentro que supuso la derrota ante los rojiblancos
articles.summary: El técnico perico lamentó la última acción del encuentro que supuso la derrota ante los rojiblancos
articles.body: El Espanyol cayó ante el Atlético de Madrid en el RCDE Stadium. Pese a firmar un buen partido, los blanquiazules vieron cómo se escapaba un punto en el minuto 90 debido al tanto de Baena. Una derrota dolorosa para un Espanyol que sigue encadenando encuentros sin lograr el triunfo. Tras el duelo, Manolo González compareció ante los medios y pese al resultado se mostró satisfecho con el trabajo y el juego de lo suyos. Eso sí, lamentó la última acción que condenó a los suyos. Fastidiado por el resultado: "Estoy fastidiado porque al final hemos hecho el partido que tocaba. El Atlético de Madrid te exige esto porque es un equipo que a nivel de transición, de balón a la espalda, uno contra uno, juego, tiene muchas soluciones. Lo he hablado con Simeone y quizás de los tres años para mí es en el que están mejor en este tipo de situaciones ofensivas. Tienes que defenderles muy bien para contraerles. Sabíamos que si el partido era largo, íbamos a tener opciones y así ha sido. La pena ha sido no meter las nuestras porque al final cuando juegas contra un rival de esta entidad tienes que meter las que tienes. Después la última situación es evitable del córner rival y te vuelve a penalizar igual que el día del Málaga y el Real Madrid". Mensaje a los futbolistas: "Tenemos que ver ellos y nosotros porque en Málaga es una situación parecida y ante el Atlético nos vuelve a pasar. Son situaciones que en el juego tienes que controlar. Estas cosas las tenemos que controlar y una vez que sales a campo abierto hay que morir". Varios goles encajados en los minutos finales: "El equipo está fastidiado, lógicamente por perder, pero sale bien a nivel de refuerzo en el juego. Salimos tocados el día del Elche porque no estamos bien en el juego y perdemos. Ahora mismo, de los dos partidos sales más reforzado que debilitado. Ante el Atlético de Madrid hemos competido a muy buen nivel contra un rival que ya vemos a qué ritmo viene en LaLiga. La única pena que se nos escapa el partido en una situación controlable". Crecer desde las buenas sensaciones: "Aún habiendo ganado al Atlético, en LaLiga todos los partidos son importantes. Tenemos que intentar crecer como equipo, ir mejorando día a día, que lo estamos haciendo, y ser cada vez más competitivos como lo hemos sido". Contento por la vuelta de Puado: "Una alegría enorme. Venía entrando muy bien, ha estado muy bien y no hay que achacarle nada, al contrario. Ha salido a ayudar, pero la pena ha sido la última acción. Todos los que han jugado se han dejado el alma y han hecho un partido muy bueno".

articles.title: Arsenal at Nottingham Forest Premier League match preview: Sharpen the axe
articles.summary: The Gunners head to Nottingham Forest in hopes of chopping down the Tricky Trees for a third win on the trot
articles.body:
Arsenal head north to take on Nottingham Forest on Sunday in the Premier League ahead of a marquee Champions League match at Bayern Munich next week.

The Gunners have enjoyed their return to action following the first international break. It hasn't been smooth sailing, but they have certainly gotten back to business since their 0-3 loss at Brighton. A nervier-than-it-needed-to-be, come-from behind win against Leeds was followed up by a dominant 3-0 win against Lille in the CL where Mikel Arteta's side looked confident and in control from start to finish.

You can't quantify or measure momentum, but you can sure as hell sense it. If there's a criticism to be laid upon the Gunners so far this season, it is that they haven't taken matches by the scruff and imposed themselves consistently when the opportunities present themselves. There have been plenty of moments of brilliance, but it hasn't felt like they have had that "oh, wait, we're the champions of England" epiphany just yet.

With that being said, you can't argue with the results. Eight wins from nine matches is excellent. Clearly, they are efficient and get the job done. Teams have brought their best against the defending title holders, which was always going to be the case. The target on their backs has never been bigger, and they have done what they needed to take care of business. But would it kill them to be just a little more assertive and stamp their names on matches?

Heading to Forest on the heels of their first one-sided performance in a while is going to be a test of their ability to seize momentum. With a big CL match away to Bayern Munich on deck, building on Wednesday's performance and capitalizing on the opportunity is paramount. Can they do it? That's the question.

Arsenal vs Nottingham Forest all-time record: 56W-24D-29L

Incomings: Liam Delap (Chelsea), Ousmane Diomande (Sporting), Daniel Muñonz (Crystal Palace), Gustavo Sá (Famalicão), Xaver Schlager (Leipzig), Steven Benda (Fulham)

Departures: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Taiwo Awoniyi (Coventry), David Carmo (Olympiacos), Jota Silva (Olympiacos), Omar Richards (Aris Saloniki), Stefan Ortega (Olympiacos), Angus Gunn (San Jose Earthquakes)

Injuries & Suspensions: Igor Jesus (calf), Nicolo Savona (knee), Nikola Milenkovic (knee), Morgan Gibbs-White (knock)

The Tricky Trees made headlines for all of the wrong reasons last season. Between their megalomaniacal owner publicly inserting himself into the Morgan Gibbs-White transfer saga, the end of the disastrous tenure of former Arsenal Head of Football Operations Edu, and enduring a coaching carousel of four (!) different managers, the product on the pitch felt like a footnote compared to the drama that permeated the club, and the results reflected that as they tumbled to a 16th place finish on the heels of a 7th place finish the season prior.

The hiring of former Crystal Palace manager Oliver Glasner over the summer looked a shrewd bit of business by Forest as they looked to right their reeling ship. After stamping his name in the Palace history books by leading the Eagles to an FA Cup in 2024/25 and a Conference League title in 25/26, his decision to part ways with the London club at the end of last season was made all the more perplexing when he agreed to manage Forest, who finished one spot below Palace and only 5 points clear of relegation.

Like too many managers before him, his Forest tenure has been underwhelming so far. Through six Premier League matches, they have struggled to secure results with one win to their name, while their Carabao Cup campaign ended swiftly after a third round loss to Leeds in August. The Elliot Anderson-sized hole in their midfield has been hard to fill after the England international left for sportswashing mega-cheats Manchester City over the summer, but that was always going to be the case.

Their early woes aren't nearly as bad as they look. No team in the league has had as much bad luck in front of goal as they have, as evidenced by 5 goals scored from an xG of 10.30. Their finishing woes are not for lack of trying; they've taken the third most shots in the league (106) while also having the joint most shots hit the post (6). The only team with a worse conversion rate have been chronic underachievers Spurs. According to Opta's expected league table , they are the season's top under-performer so far, with the stat house having them theoretically 12 spots higher in third place.

Their defensive returns have been equally as frustrating. They have faced only one shot (65) more than Arsenal, who have given up a league-low 64, while allowing only 22 shots on target, which is third-best in the PL and only three more than the Gunners. They have allowed a respectable 8 goals, but their inability to finish their dinner in the attack has undercut an otherwise solid defense.

The availability of talisman Gibbs-White could be a potential problem for both sides. He suffered a muscular injury last week in Forest's 1-3 defeat at Crystal Palace with his fitness for Sunday uncertain. Glasner's pre-match comments seem to indicate that his injury isn't serious and that he has a decent chance of making the match-day squad. With attacker Igor Jesus already out, Glasner may be forced to take a gamble on a not-fully-fit Gibbs-White, and for good reason. He is one of the league's top facilitators so far, with the second most chances created (17), most big chances created (7), and most expected assists (1.87).

Nottingham Forest are a team that is due a course correction on both ends of the pitch. Hopefully, that begins after Sunday.

Where they will look to make a difference against Arsenal will be in the air and shooting from distance. They have won 52.8% of their aerial duels and have the second-most attempted headers with 20, bolstered by Morgan Gibbs-White and Neco Williams providing the second and third-most successful crosses across the Prem this season. Their penchant for long shots could trouble David Raya and the Gunners' defense with over 40 shots from outside the box this season. Arsenal have struggled with long shots, having conceded 40% of their goals from distance. If they take them early and often, they could potentially find some success on the score sheet.

Arsenal's biggest issue this season has been their slow starts. In eight matches across all competitions, the Gunners have scored a first-half goal in only 3 of them, with 5 of their 18 goals coming before halftime. They have also fallen behind in three of their last four Premier League matches before coming from behind to win two. Arsenal are fortunate in that their depth and overall quality gives them an edge as games wear on, but leaving it late and having to claw out of deficits is an awful trait to sustain for player and fan health alike.

The last two matches between the Gunners and Forest at the City Ground have ended in goalless draws, and the Gunners have won just once in their last six visits. Getting off the mark early has to be a priority if they want to leave with all 3 points and keep pace with Manchester City.

articles.title: ¿El PSG saca tajada por jugar en la Ligue 1?
articles.standfirst: Enzo Maresca, entrenador del club inglés, afirmó tras la dura derrota que la ventaja del equipo de Luis Enrique es que el bajo nivel de la Ligue 1 le permite rotar más
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca, entrenador del club inglés, afirmó tras la dura derrota que la ventaja del equipo de Luis Enrique es que el bajo nivel de la Ligue 1 le permite rotar más
articles.body: El PSG ha salido en defensa de la Ligue 1 tras las declaraciones del entrenador del City, Enzo Maresca, que para justificar el duro correctivo de su rival en la Champions habló del bajo nivel de la Ligue 1 con respecto a la Premier. "El PSG tiene la oportunidad de descansar a algunos de sus mejores jugadores antes de cada partido de la Champions League. Para nosotros es un poco diferente, especialmente cuando tienes que ir a Anfield", apuntó. Luis Enrique fue el primero en responder ayer en la sala de prensa: "Es el ruido habitual que rodea a un equipo como el PSG. Antes de llegar aquí, se decía que el París nunca había ganado la Liga de Campeones porque la Ligue 1 no tenía el nivel suficiente. ¡Eso es lo que oía incluso antes de llegar! Y hoy en día, mucha gente se queja diciendo que tenemos ventaja porque la Ligue 1 es más débil. Para nosotros es difícil ganar, y eso es lo que queremos hacer". Cierto es que para justificar los enormes batacazos del PSG en la etapa de los Neymar, Mbappé, Messi, Verratti o Ibrahimovic se argumentaba que el equipo no estaba acostumbrado a competir cada jornada y que por eso se veía sorprendido en los grande duelos. El nivel de la Ligue 1 no puede considerarse un hándicap cuando el Paris Saint-Germain pierde en la Liga de Campeones y una ventaja cuando gana. El mismo campeonato era un hándicap en 2020-2021 y se presenta como una ventaja en 2026: ambas interpretaciones no pueden coexistir. Muchos de los futbolistas que han pasado por la Ligue 1 cree que no se valora la competición como merece. Gabriel Gudmundsson, exjugador del Lille, actualmente en el Leeds, afirmó en su primer año en Inglaterra que "la Ligue 1 es una liga muy física. Es una buena liga, mejor de lo que muchos piensan. Hasta ahora, no hay ninguna diferencia en el plano físico con la Premier". Salomon Kalou, exjugador del Lille y del Chelsea, habló en los mismos términos: "La Ligue 1 está infravalorada. La gente habla del PSG, pero la liga cuenta con muchos equipos fuertes y produce un talento increíble. Basta con mirar a los jugadores que han salido de Francia: están por toda Europa. El Lille y el Lens están demostrando que no todo gira en torno al PSG". El PSG disputó 67 partidos en 2025, incluido el Mundial de Clubes. Los once titulares comparados del PSG y del Manchester City acumulaban, respectivamente, 7.059 y 7.043 minutos de juego: una diferencia de tan solo 16 minutos en total. Para realizar una comparación justa, hay que tener en cuenta toda la temporada y todas las competiciones. Los onces titulares del PSG y del Manchester City acumulan prácticamente el mismo tiempo de juego desde el inicio de la temporada. Criticar al PSG basándose en una supuesta ventaja de frescura física carece de fundamento si no se consideran todos los datos. Tanto en Inglaterra como en Alemania, el Arsenal y el Bayern de Múnich ganaron sus campeonatos nacionales mientras alcanzaban, respectivamente, la final y las semifinales de la Liga de Campeones. Ser competitivo en varios frentes es perfectamente posible. La gestión de los partidos depende de la situación deportiva de cada club. Tampoco entienden en París las quejas de Maresca cuando sobran medios económicos en la Premier. Sus ingresos audiovisuales son muy superiores a los de la Ligue 1, y estos recursos contribuyen a financiar plantillas más amplias y competitivas. Los derechos televisivos, los presupuestos, los salarios y los traspasos deben formar parte de la comparación: contar con una plantilla amplia tiene un coste. "Si queremos hablar de ventajas estructurales, hablemos también de los recursos financieros, y no únicamente del calendario", responden.

articles.title: El Stuttgart muere en la orilla en Hamburgo antes de recibir al Atlético
articles.standfirst: Un golazo de Muheim en el 88' provoca la derrota de los de Sebastian Hoeness
articles.summary: Un golazo de Muheim en el 88' provoca la derrota de los de Sebastian Hoeness
articles.body: el Stuttgart, rival del Atlético, se plantó en Hamburgo con cuatro cambios respecto al once que ganó al Slovan Bratislava (0-3) en Champions. Entró Seimen por Bredlow bajo palos y Karazor, Leweling y Demirovic ocuparon el lugar de Prömel, Führich y Pejcinovic. No le fue bien. Cayeron 1-0 en su visita al Volksparkstadion. Empezó dominando, eso sí. Pudo marcar, incluso, en el 6'. Heuer Fernandes desvió un tiro desde la frontal de Vagnoman y Capaldo evitó que Demirovic transformara el rechace. El propio Demirovic conectó un disparo en el 27', tras una contra, que salió rozando el poste. Entre medias, en el 26', pudo marcar el 1-0 el Hamburgo. Lo evitó, con una gran parada, Seimen. El meta desvió un córner que prolongó Bornauw y desvió Fábio Vieira en boca de gol. La ocasión más clara antes del descanso la tuvo Undaz en el 39'. Ganó línea de fondo Leweling y encontró al internacional alemán. Sin embargo, su disparo se estrelló contra el poste izquierdo. Fue el Hamburgo quien, tras el descanso, merceió el gol. Yussuf Poulsen conectó un cabezazo que se marchó junto al poste en el 48' y, acto seguido, en el 53', se sacó de la manga un obús que se estrelló contra el larguero. Respondió el Stuttgart con un testarazo de Demirovic que salió fuera en el 53' -el ex del Alavés terminó rompiéndose la camiseta- y un disparo de Undav, en el 58', que desvió Heuer Fernandes con una buena estirada. No era el día del Stuttgart. Pejcinovic remató fuera, en el 85', un gran pase atrás de Leo Sauer. Para colmo, Miro Muheim anotó el 1-0 para el Hamburgo en el 88'. Recibió de Zakaria El Ouahdi y conectó un tremendo zurdazo cruzado desde la frontal. Imparable para Seimen. Explotaba el Volksparkstadion para desesperación de un Stuttgart, que se queda decimotercero con seis puntos. El 'HSV', por su parte, es octavo con nueve.
